surface_mechanism_description: The surface chemistry involves ligand exchange reactions where the WF6-terminated surface reacts with NH3 in a ligand exchange reaction to produce W-N bonds and HF as by-product. The triethylboron-terminated surface reacts with WF6 via transmetalation to form W-C bonds and liberates fluoroboron species. The ammonia-terminated surface complex provides adsorption sites for the Lewis acid B sC2H5d3.
